3.Monthly Claim Amount Trend¶

In [35]:
import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

# Convert claim date
claims['Date of Claim'] = pd.to_datetime(
    claims['Date of Claim'],
    errors='coerce'
)

# Extract month
claims['Month'] = claims['Date of Claim'].dt.month

# Combine all years by month
monthly_claims = (
    claims.groupby('Month')['Claim Amount']
    .sum()
    .reindex(range(1, 13), fill_value=0)
)

month_names = [
    'Jan', 'Feb', 'Mar', 'Apr', 'May', 'Jun',
    'Jul', 'Aug', 'Sep', 'Oct', 'Nov', 'Dec'
]

# Convert values to Millions
monthly_claims_m = monthly_claims / 1_000_000

# Print values in M
print(monthly_claims_m.round(2))

# Create chart
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(12, 6))

ax.plot(
    month_names,
    monthly_claims_m.values,
    marker='o'
)

plt.title('Claim Amount by Month')
plt.xlabel('Month')
plt.ylabel('Total Claim Amount (M)')

# Add M values
for i, value in enumerate(monthly_claims_m.values):
    ax.annotate(
        f'{value:.2f}M',
        (i, value),
        xytext=(0, 8),
        textcoords='offset points',
        ha='center',
        fontsize=8
    )

plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()

Month
1     22.01
2     20.79
3     21.17
4     21.13
5     20.93
6     21.27

4.Premium Amount by Policy Type¶

In [36]:
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

# Premium amount by policy type
premium_by_type = (
    policies.groupby('Policy Type')['Premium Amount']
    .sum()
    .sort_values(ascending=False)
)

# Convert to Millions
premium_by_type_m = premium_by_type / 1_000_000

# Print actual values
print(premium_by_type_m.round(2))

# Create chart
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(10, 6))

bars = ax.bar(
    premium_by_type_m.index,
    premium_by_type_m.values
)

plt.title('Premium Amount by Policy Type')
plt.xlabel('Policy Type')
plt.ylabel('Total Premium Amount (M)')

# Add values on bars
for bar, value in zip(bars, premium_by_type_m.values):
    ax.annotate(
        f'{value:.2f}M',
        (bar.get_x() + bar.get_width() / 2, bar.get_height()),
        xytext=(0, 6),
        textcoords='offset points',
        ha='center',
        fontsize=9
    )

plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()

Policy Type
Health      1.36
Life        1.34
Property    1.31
Auto        1.25
Name: Premium Amount, dtype: float64

    claims.groupby('Reason for Claim')['Claim Amount']
    .sum()
    .sort_values(ascending=False)
)

    top10_m.index,
    top10_m.values
)

    ax.text(
        bar.get_x() + bar.get_width()/2,
        bar.get_height(),
        f'{value:.2f}M',
        ha='center',
        va='bottom',

    )

plt.show()

6.Claim Amount Distribution - Histogram¶

In [62]:
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

# Convert Claim Amount to Millions
claim_amount_m = claims['Claim Amount'] / 1_000_000

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(10, 6))

# Create histogram
counts, bins, patches = ax.hist(
    claim_amount_m,
    bins=15,
    edgecolor='black'
)

plt.title('Claim Amount Distribution')
plt.xlabel('Claim Amount (M)')
plt.ylabel('Number of Claims')

# Add count values on each bar
for count, patch in zip(counts, patches):
    if count > 0:
        ax.text(
            patch.get_x() + patch.get_width() / 2,
            count,
            f'{int(count)}',
            ha='center',
            va='bottom',
            fontsize=9
        )

plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()

Key Insights¶

  • Total premium collected is ₹5.26M, while total claim amount is ₹251.38M, indicating high claim exposure in the dataset.
  • Claim amount is highest in December (₹22.09M) and lowest in September (₹19.30M).
  • Claim volumes are fairly consistent across the claim-amount ranges, with no major concentration.
  • Health insurance has the highest policy count (1,316) and the highest premium amount (₹1.36M).
  • Payment performance is almost balanced: 2,516 successful vs 2,484 failed payments.
  • Claim status is distributed across Approved (1,712), Pending (1,650), and Denied (1,638), showing a significant pending/denied portion.
  • Policy renewal is also balanced, with 1,685 not renewed, 1,668 renewed, and 1,647 pending.

Recommendations¶

Recommendations¶

  • Improve payment success by investigating the causes of the 2,484 failed payments.
  • Focus on Health policies to maintain strong premium performance and manage claim exposure.
  • Investigate the high claim amounts during December and identify seasonal claim patterns.
  • Reduce the pending claim backlog through faster claim assessment and processing.
  • Improve policy renewal through targeted customer retention campaigns.
  • Analyze claim reasons and identify recurring causes to support better risk management.
